note: 9 rust-doctor diagnostics were consolidated into 6 findings (the four tests/registry.rs near-duplicate diagnostics were merged into GR-012 because they share the same root cause and remediation; the other tests/* diagnostics were kept separate by file). All 9 diagnostics are individually addressable by ID within the findings list.

findings.title: GuardrailDecision enum is not #[non_exhaustive] — external matchers will break on new variants
findings.description: GuardrailDecision is re-exported at crate root (`pub use decision::{GuardrailDecision, Replacement}`) and matched externally by the harness and downstream callers. Adding a new variant (e.g. `Defer`, `Quarantine`) is a breaking change for every external match arm. The enum is the public decision vocabulary of the entire guardrail pipeline and warrants forward-compat.
findings.trigger: Any downstream code matching on `GuardrailDecision::*` exhaustively; library upgrade adding a fifth variant.
findings.current_code:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuardrailDecision {
    Allow,
    Sanitize(Replacement),
    Block { reason: String, class: ErrorClass },
    Warn { reason: String },
}
findings.suggested_fix: Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the enum (and to `Replacement` if its field set is also unstable). Document the variant-set policy in the module doc.

findings.title: screen_session_input silently degrades to redact-only when tail_start > events.len()
findings.description: When `tail_start` exceeds `events.len()`, `tail_start.min(events.len())..` yields an empty slice; `find_map` returns `None`; `blocking` becomes `None`; `screen_user_messages` then runs with `blocking = None` — every Block degrades to redaction. This is the same shape as `redact_session_input` (the documented salvage face), but it is reached via the WRONG code path (a caller error rather than an explicit grace-turn). A caller that passes a stale `tail_start` (e.g. a session whose log shrank after a compaction or split) silently turns every blocked user paste into a redacted prompt instead of ending the turn. The behavior is undetectable at the call site.
findings.trigger: Caller passes tail_start past end of events after a split/compaction shrinks the log; also reachable by any test/feed that mishandles tail_start.
findings.current_code:
let blocking = events[tail_start.min(events.len())..]
    .iter()
    .enumerate()
    .rev()
    .find_map(|(rel, r)| user_text(&r.event).map(|_| tail_start + rel));
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) return `SessionInputScreen::Blocked("tail_start out of range".into())` when `tail_start > events.len()`, or (b) at minimum emit a `tracing::warn!` with `tail_start`, `events.len()` so the failure mode is observable. Prefer (a) since (b) leaves the silent degradation in place.

findings.title: Wide-and-shallow adversarial tool args bypass the depth cap (memory DoS)
findings.description: `MAX_SCAN_DEPTH = 32` caps recursion but NOT branching. A pathologically shallow-but-wide JSON payload — a single `{ "items": [<1M short strings>] }` — still recurses 2 levels deep and processes every leaf. Each leaf allocates: (a) a String for the rebuilt Vec, (b) a BoxFuture for the recursion call (every level), (c) a `serde_json::Map` for the parent, (d) `process_outbound` does its own allocations (placeholder extraction, regex scans). The total memory scales linearly with leaf count and an attacker controls the tool-arg payload at the agent loop's hottest dispatch path.
findings.trigger: Any tool that accepts free-form JSON args (bash exec, file write with metadata) fed a 1M-element array via model prompt-injection or user paste.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `MAX_SCAN_NODES: usize = 65_536` counter incremented at every entry; on exceed, Block with class Unexpected (same shape as the depth overflow). Mirrors the depth cap rationale: cap rather than scan partial tree.

findings.title: SecretError Display still echoes user-supplied name in audit log after Block reason was sanitized
findings.description: The Block reason path was deliberately hardened against vault-namespace enumeration by stripping the requested secret name (see the long comment in the `SecretResolutionFailed` arm). However, `tracing::warn!(error = %e, ...)` is called immediately above and `SecretError::NotFound(name).to_string()` echoes `name` verbatim (per `SecretError` Display impls in src/secrets/types.rs). If the audit log is ever shipped to a UI panel, the orchestrator's `room_author` log capture, or any user-visible channel, the enumeration side channel re-opens. The block-reason fix is a one-sided partial sanitization — the same secret name still reaches operators.
findings.trigger: Any audit-log forwarder (UI panel, alert channel) that exposes the warn! line; a future change to `AuditEntry::detail` that surfaces warn context.
findings.suggested_fix: Log a redacted form of `e`. Either pass the pre-classified `variant` string only (already provided), or redact the Display output: `let redacted = variant; tracing::warn!(error_kind = redacted, ...)`. Document that the operator-side path can include name ONLY via an explicit elevated-access debug! at trace level.

findings.title: evaluate_input / evaluate_output in registry are near-identical 238-line bodies
findings.description: rust-doctor flagged the two `evaluate_input` / `evaluate_output` methods as 238 nodes of duplicated structure (only the trait method invoked inside the loop differs). The divergence that previously broke parity (the tool-call twin compared payloads, the others checked warns) sat 20 lines below the correct predicate in the same file — the duplication is exactly what hid the bug. Factor into one helper that takes a closure `f: impl Fn(&Arc<G>, &str) -> Future<GuardrailDecision>`.
findings.trigger: Adding a new guardrail surface (4th trait method) or new decision handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `async fn chain<G, F, Fut>(&self, list: &[Arc<G>], initial: &str, eval: F) -> GuardrailDecision where F: Fn(&G, &str) -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = GuardrailDecision>`. The tool_call variant needs an extra Value-typed branch but the input/output pair becomes one call.

findings.title: evaluate_tool_call calls serde_json::to_string(args) on serialization failure, silently sending ORIGINAL un-sanitized args
findings.description: When `rewritten=true` but `serde_json::to_string(&current)` fails, the code falls back to `args.to_string()` (the ORIGINAL un-redacted args) and returns it inside `GuardrailDecision::Sanitize`. The caller is then expected to use this text as the tool args. The redaction that already fired is silently undone at this seam. `Value` to_string is theoretically infallible but the seam exists and could mask a future bug (e.g. an `f64::NaN` round-trip).
findings.trigger: Any pathological Value that fails to_string; in practice dead code, but the shape is a defense-in-depth hole.
findings.current_code:
settle_chain(
    rewritten,
    warns,
    serde_json::to_string(&current).unwrap_or_else(|_| args.to_string()),  // <-- falls back to ORIGINAL
)
findings.suggested_fix: On serialization failure: `tracing::error!(...)` + return `GuardrailDecision::Block { reason: "guardrail serialization failed; refusing to pass un-sanitized args".into(), class: ErrorClass::Unexpected }`. Mirror the contract used in `PiiSecretsGuardrail::evaluate_tool_call` which already does this correctly (`Guardrail serialization failed: {e}`).

findings.title: disable_all audit log conflates operator action with hostile sub-module action
findings.description: `disable_all()` is callable from anywhere an `Arc<GuardrailRegistry>` is reachable. The audit log uses `current_scope().map(|s| s.owner_user_id).unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into())` — this collapses two operationally distinct callers into one log line: (a) a CLI admin toggling it via an operator path where scope is intentionally unset (logs as 'unknown'), and (b) a hostile sub-module / plugin / callback whose scope is set to its own (logs as that user). The 'unknown' outcome is also the default for any future async context that forgot to seed scope. After the fact, an operator cannot tell a legitimate disable from a compromised one without other signals.
findings.trigger: Forensic analysis of any production disable event; hostile plugin disabled guardrails after bypassing scope capture.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the span/site (e.g. `tracing::Span::current()` location, or a caller-supplied reason via a `disable_all_with_reason(&str)` API). Log `actor_present: bool` so `None` (scope absent) is distinguishable from `Some(unknown)`. Consider restricting `disable_all` to admin-only via an existing scope guard instead of leaving it open to any `Arc` holder.

findings.title: screen_session_input slice indexing at events[tail_start.min(events.len())..] flagged by clippy; semantically a silent-fail-open path
findings.description: clippy::indexing_slicing flagged `events[tail_start.min(events.len())..]` — the `.min()` does prevent panic but clippy cannot statically verify that. The semantic problem (not the panic) is GR-002: a stale tail_start silently degrades to redact-only. Either fix the indexing with `.get(..).unwrap_or(&[])` AND fix the silent fail-open together, or document that 'tail_start > len() is a legitimate caller signal for redact-only' and add a test pinning it.
findings.trigger: See GR-002 trigger; also clippy run in CI.
findings.current_code:
let blocking = events[tail_start.min(events.len())..]
    .iter()
    .enumerate()
    .rev()
    .find_map(|(rel, r)| user_text(&r.event).map(|_| tail_start + rel));

findings.title: Empty builder + Default derive produces an Allow-everything registry, indistinguishable from a misconfigured one
findings.description: `GuardrailRegistryBuilder` is `#[derive(Default)]`, which means a `GuardrailRegistry::default()` exists. Building with no guardrails yields a registry where every surface returns Allow — operationally indistinguishable from a misconfigured production deploy where the intended PII guardrail was never wired. Combined with the `Option<Arc<GuardrailRegistry>>` storage in `HarnessDeps`, an unwrap-default-here is one path away from silently disabled guardrails in production.
findings.trigger: A test or builder that forgets to call `with_input(PiiSecretsGuardrail::...)`; a future Default::default() at a new call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) drop the `Default` impl so `GuardrailRegistryBuilder::default()` is unavailable and every caller must use `.builder().with_input(...).with_output(...).build()` explicitly, or (b) make `build()` panic / log a warn when all three lists are empty (fail-loud at construction, not at runtime).

findings.title: PII redacted text changes wire type from Number to String in tool args — caller schema breakage
findings.description: When a JSON Number leaf (e.g. an 11-digit phone or 16-digit card PAN expressed as `1234567890123456`) hits the redact path, the code falls back to `Value::String(scanned)` after `parse::<serde_json::Number>()` fails. The tool arg wire shape flips from Number to String; a downstream tool with a strict schema (`{"type": "number"}`) will now reject the call or silently coerce. The accompanying `tracing::warn!` is fine for the audit trail but does not prevent the runtime breakage. A model that legitimately wrote a numeric arg now gets an unexplained tool error and may retry with another secret-shaped number, amplifying the detection cost.
findings.trigger: Model emits a phone number or card number as JSON Number in any tool arg; Luhn-checked 16-digit values commonly serialize as numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: On type-change, return `GuardrailDecision::Block { reason: "numeric arg redacted to string; rejecting to preserve schema".into(), class: ErrorClass::Fixable }` instead of silently changing the shape. This surfaces the redaction to the model as a content-policy block (it can re-emit a different shape) rather than papering over it.

findings.title: Regex pattern catalog is case-sensitive for vendor prefixes; bypass via mixed case / homoglyphs
findings.description: Patterns are matched on raw bytes without case folding: `AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}` requires uppercase; `gh[pousr]_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36,}` matches both cases but does not match homoglyphs. The `(?i:Bearer)` prefix handles one case but other prefixes (`sk-ant-`, `sk-proj-`, `glpat-`, `AIza`) are case-sensitive. Real attackers frequently inject `Sk-Ant-...`, `akiA...`, or Unicode lookalikes (`Ｓｋ-` fullwidth). The pii/rules/api_key.rs uses `(?i)` for the Bearer prefix only — same gap. This is a partial detection bypass for the most common evasion: lowercasing / case-flipping the prefix.
findings.trigger: Attacker pastes `Sk-Ant-abcdef...` or fullwidth-`Ｓｋ-ant-` to evade the egress guard.
findings.current_code:
("sk_proj", r"\bsk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),
("sk_ant", r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),
("aws_akia", r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),
("github_pat", r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
("openai_sk", r"\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}"),
("google_api", r"AIza[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]{35}"),
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(?i)` prefix to every vendor-secret pattern (or add a `(?i:sk|ant)` preflight scan for the prefix portion before the bounded quantifier runs). For homoglyphs: add a Unicode NFKD normalization step (`unicode-normalization`) before regex matching, and run a separate confusables check on the matched prefix. Document the residual gap explicitly if normalization is deferred.

findings.title: Six near-duplicate test stubs across tests/ registry.rs (88% body similarity)
findings.description: Six test functions in tests/registry.rs duplicate the `AllowAll` / `AlwaysBlock` / `SanitizeSecret` / `WarnOnly` / `SilentScrubber` stub shape and the registry-construction boilerplate. Three functions at lines 306-326, 328-348, 350-371 share an 88% body — the duplication increases with each test added. Also flagged: tests/input.rs:31 + tests/output.rs:32 + tests/registry.rs:536 share an 81% body (input/output/registry surface twin tests).
findings.trigger: Adding a new guardrail test (any new stub type will need boilerplate refactor).
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a `tests/registry/common.rs` (or a `mod testkit { ... }` in tests/mod.rs) with `fn allow_all() -> Arc<AllowAll>`, `fn always_block() -> Arc<AlwaysBlock>`, etc., and a `fn registry_with(handlers: &[(...)]) -> GuardrailRegistry` builder. The 306-371 cluster becomes 3 short tests calling common helpers.

findings.title: Test pair input_does_not_resolve_placeholder / output_does_not_resolve_placeholder shares 82% body
findings.description: The two tests assert that the input and output surfaces do not resolve placeholders. Bodies differ only in the input string ("hello {{secret:test_key}}" vs "LLM said {{secret:test_key}}") and the surface called. The shape is shared and the contract is identical ('placeholder must not appear in Allow/Warn/Sanitize text on the non-tool surfaces'); the duplication is acceptable for a focused regression test, but the second test's weakened assertion (`if let Sanitize ...`) silently bypasses the same invariant if a future change returns Allow on the output surface.
findings.trigger: Adding a third non-resolving surface test, or a future regression that returns Allow on output (currently under-tested).
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) extract a `fn assert_does_not_resolve(dec: &GuardrailDecision)` helper that handles all four variants symmetrically, or (b) tighten the output test to use the same `match` form as the input test. Pick (a) — the helper makes future regressions across all surfaces one assertion.

findings.title: Test pair tool_call_resolves_placeholder / tool_call_unknown_secret_blocks (87% body)
findings.description: Two tool_call tests share the setup `guard(true) + json!({command: "echo {{secret:NAME}}"})` and the eval+assert structure, differing only in the placeholder name and the asserted variant. The duplication is small but compounds with the input/output pair above into 4 near-identical tests — a candidate for `assert_tool_call_resolves(name)` / `assert_tool_call_blocks(name)` helpers.
findings.trigger: Adding a third tool_call surface test (e.g. resolving with WARN-leak detector advice).
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a `fn assert_tool_call_decision(guard: &PiiSecretsGuardrail, name: &str, expect: fn(&GuardrailDecision))` helper.

findings.title: tests/bench.rs noop_input / noop_output duplicate 88% body
findings.description: The two noop benchmarks share the loop, threshold check, and assertion message verbatim, differing only in `evaluate_input` vs `evaluate_output`. The duplication is acceptable for a smoke benchmark but is a candidate for a small `fn assert_noop_budget(d: Duration)` helper that centralizes the threshold + message.
findings.trigger: Adjusting the budget threshold or adding a third noop surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `fn assert_noop_budget(elapsed: Duration, surface: &str, iters: usize)` and have both tests call it.

findings.title: Public traits have no #[non_exhaustive] on associated struct variants (Replacement, Sanitize payload)
findings.description: Replacement's `text` and `source` fields are stable today but the struct is part of the public decision API and is likely to grow (audit metadata, confidence score, rule id). Adding any field is a breaking change for downstream destructuring. Mark `Replacement` `#[non_exhaustive]` and provide a constructor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `#[non_exhaustive]` and a `pub fn new(text: String, source: impl Into<String>) -> Self` constructor. Update internal call sites to use the constructor.

findings.title: Disable-actor log uses 'unknown' for both absent scope and unattested callers — operationally indistinguishable
findings.description: Sub-finding of GR-007: `actor = current_scope().map(...).unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into())` cannot distinguish 'no scope context at all' from 'scope set but owner_user_id is the literal string "unknown"' — and the latter is reachable because `unwrap_or_else` collapses all None values. Even more operationally: any future code path that seeds a default ScopeAttribution with owner_user_id = "unknown" would log identically to the absent-scope case. Recommend explicit enum: `actor: enum { Unscoped, Scoped(String) }` for unambiguous triage.
findings.trigger: Forensic review of disable_all log lines; any UI surface that summarizes 'who disabled guardrails'.
findings.suggested_fix: Log `actor_present: bool` alongside `actor_user: Option<&str>` so absence is preserved.

top_risks: GR-002 (P1, security-fail-open): silent fail-open when tail_start > events.len() — entire turn proceeds with redacted prompt instead of blocking
GR-003 (P1, denial-of-service): wide-and-shallow tool-arg JSON triggers unbounded allocation on the agent hot path (depth cap alone is insufficient)
GR-004 (P1, side-channel): SecretError Display re-leaks the user-supplied secret name in audit log, partially undoing the Block-reason sanitization
GR-001 (P1, api-hazard): GuardrailDecision is a public enum without #[non_exhaustive] — a single new variant breaks every external match arm
negative_findings: No ReDoS vulnerability detected: all SECRET_PATTERN_SOURCES patterns are bounded or use bounded character classes; no nested quantifiers.
No hardcoded test secret in production code: stub resolver in delegation_tests lives behind #[cfg(test)] and returns a clearly-marked placeholder value.
Custom user-supplied regex correctly uses safe_regex::bounded_builder, preventing ReDoS via config-driven patterns.
Post-substitution leak re-scan (runtime_guard.rs:281) correctly closes the resolved-secret-echo bypass; covered by dedicated regression test.
PII engine covers a wider catalog (gho_, github_pat_, sk-or-v1-, etc.) than the egress leak detector; the egress detector's coverage gap is mitigated by defense-in-depth with the PII engine.
